messages:
tasha: FYI I opened a PR that bumps the shared schema and also centralizes a couple CODEOWNERS entries: https://git.redwood/corp/mono-repo/pull/482

miguel: Looks like it touches api, runtime, and infra-config. By default each repo's CODEOWNERS need to approve. Which teams are listed as owners?

tasha: api -> @team-api, runtime -> @eng-runtime, infra-config -> @eng-infra. I added @eng-platform as a fallback in the central CODEOWNERS. Question is: do we need explicit owner approvals from each file, or is a single team lead approval enough?

soph: For changes that modify CODEOWNERS we usually require someone who is actually listed in the CODEOWNERS file to approve. Team leads can approve other code changes, but CODEOWNERS edits are treated as ownership decisions. Ping the people listed in the file.

ben: Is this blocking a release? If it's urgent we can request platform-oncall to rubber-stamp, but that's an exception (hotfix flow).

tasha: Not critical but would like to land before Friday's release cut. Prefer not to split into 3 PRs if we can avoid it. Can we do async approvals?

miguel: Two practical paths: 1) split into per-repo PRs so each owner reviews their piece, or 2) keep mono PR and get explicit approves from the listed owners in each repo. I can review the runtime bits. @soph can you take infra-config? @ben can you confirm platform is OK being a fallback owner?

soph: I can take infra-config. Quick ask: when touching CODEOWNERS, please add a short rationale + list of people you pinged in the PR body so it's auditable. Also include the exact diff snippet.

ben: Platform is fine being fallback, but our policy requires at least two platform engineers to sign off when we add fallback ownership. @tasha, add a small consent checklist in the PR that names the two approvers.

platform-oncall-bot: Reminder: merging changes to CODEOWNERS triggers the pipeline check `codeowners/safety-check`. Make sure CI passes before merge.

nick: Saw the ping — I'll review the api changes tomorrow AM.

lina: I reviewed infra-config and left a tiny path-nit. otherwise LGTM from infra side.

harper: I approve the runtime update. left one non-blocking nit re: version suffix.

tasha: Thanks all — I'll add the approval checklist and a short rationale to the PR, tag the two platform approvers per policy, and aim to merge after Fri 10:00am PST if no objections. If we need faster, I'll split out the CODEOWNERS change into a separate PR.

miguel: :thumbsup: sounds good. Thanks for coordinating.
